research_rationale:
EO 10718 (22 FR 4632, signed 1957-06-27) has three sections: section 1 delegates to the Secretary of State the authority vested in the President by section 1745 of the Revised Statutes (22 U.S.C. 1201) to prescribe rates or tariffs of fees for official services at embassies, legations and consulates, to designate what are official services, and to adapt the rates to each post; section 2 provides that the order does not itself amend or end existing rates but includes authority to amend, supersede or terminate them and to prescribe implementing regulations; section 3 requires publication in the Federal Register. The Federal Register pages also print Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1957 (abolition of the Reconstruction Finance Corporation) after the order; the dossier inventory treated sections of that plan as clauses of this order, so the inventory is corrected to the order's own three sections. The held original has no sunset, condition or own-terms end. The authority statute is held and has not lapsed: the held U.S. Code text of 22 U.S.C. 4219 (R.S. 1745; formerly 22 U.S.C. 1201) still authorizes the President to prescribe the rates and prints Ex. Ord. No. 10718 in its Executive Documents note; the held eCFR authority citation of 22 CFR part 22 (amended through 2026-10-21) cites E.O. 10718, and a held 2021 Federal Register rule describes 22 U.S.C. 4219 as implemented through Executive Order 10718. the bounded machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage and show no amendment, revocation or supersession.
